newsitem.title: FRANCE: Leo Burnett wins top Lions award for Mercedes ad.
newsitem.headline: Leo Burnett wins top Lions award for Mercedes ad.

text.p: A wordless advertisement for a Mercedes Benz car created by the London office of Leo Burnett won the top award in the Press & Poster category at the 1997 International Advertising Festival here.
The festival, now in its 44th year, honors the creative side of the advertising industry.
The 20-member, all-male jury voted unanimously to award the Grand Prix to the Mercedes "Skidmarks" ad.

Festival Director Charles Sciberras said the lack of women on the jury reflects the lack of highly ranked women in the advertising industry. But he said he would not expect to see different results in choosing winners if there had been women on the jury, insisting that the preferences between men and women in advertising are not significant.

"The industry always moons and says you should have more women," Sciberras told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday, following the Tuesday night awards ceremony. "We say, promote There are two women on this year's 21-member jury for the film awards, and Sciberras noted that past juries have also included women.

Festival representatives in each country nominate three jurors each, with Sciberras making the final jury selection. The countries composing the jury rotate from year to year, with a core group of western countries always contributing jurors.

"In the United States, United Kingdom, Germany -- where there are women good enough to put on the jury, the festival representatives put them on," Sciberras said. The two women jurors on the film panel this year are from Britain and Germany.
But Sciberras noted that there are no highly ranked women in the advertising industry in countries such as France, Spain, Korea and Japan.
Jurors must hold high-level positions in their agencies, in order to maintain the stature of the awards, Sciberras said.
Geoff Thompson, worldwide creative director for Foote, Cone & Belding and a juror in 1996, noted that even in the United States there are extremely few women creative directors.

The Press & Poster category drew a record 6,600 entries, up 35 percent from 1996. Sciberras said he expects the number of entries for the category to stabilise at about 9,600 in the year 2000. The Press & Poster category was created in 1992, adding to the existing awards for film adverts.
Advertising agencies choose their own entrants for the competitions and may enter as many ads as they want. There is a fee for each entry.

Britain was the top award winner in the Press & Poster category this year, with 31 awards, including the Grand Prix and five Gold. Spain won 19 awards, including one Gold; Brazil took 18 awards, with five Gold; the U.S. took 13 awards, with six Gold; South Africa had 10 awards, with seven Gold; Australia took five awards; Singapore had five awards, with one Gold; Canada had four, with two Gold; Argentina two; France two; Japan two; Portugal two, with one Gold; Hungary one; Korea one Gold; Netherlands one, and Norway one.
